Semi-classical Hawking evaporation is expected to break down at some point in a black hole's evolution as the effects of quantum gravity become important. In particular, it has been argued that the so-called memory-burden effect could cause black holes to become stabilized by the information that they carry, thereby suppressing the rate at which they undergo Hawking evaporation. input.assessment:
Memory burden, if it halts Hawking evaporation by the time a black hole has lost about half its mass, would let primordial black holes far lighter than the standard evaporation threshold survive to the present day, and the 2024 proposal by Alexandre, Dvali, and Koutsangelas (Physical Review D 110, 036004, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14069) identified the 10^4 to 10^10 gram range as a newly viable window in which such holes could constitute all of the dark matter. The claim has since become the site of a live dispute. A 2025 reanalysis by Montefalcone, Hooper, Freese, Kelso, Kühnel, and Sandick (Physical Review D 113, 023524, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21005) recalculated the same big bang nucleosynthesis and cosmic microwave background bounds and found that the window survives only if the transition from semiclassical to burdened evaporation is practically instantaneous; under a continuous transition, [[claim:65f3b122-10de-46ec-907c-e4543c78dc83|BBN and recombination exclude everything lighter than about 4×10^16 grams from being all or most of the dark matter]], well above the proposed window. Later crossover studies reach the same qualitative conclusion with independent modeling choices, [[claim:a236aad5-5536-4caa-8957-34c62173a667|tightening the bounds and capping the window's dark matter fraction at roughly a percent in the multiplicative-crossover case]], and analyses of the transition itself find that present-day particle fluxes force the onset to be near-instantaneous for a population of this abundance.

The verdict is contested, with the burden of argument currently on the affirmative side. The window is a conditional prediction: it holds given [[claim:7ab3b712-47d8-4087-a797-6c90bc9ae58f|survival of memory-burdened holes across cosmic time]] and given [[claim:bb218573-b19d-49ae-b1e3-87fe8e234032|an effectively instantaneous handover from semiclassical to burdened evaporation]], and neither ingredient has been established; the abrupt-onset premise is the specific point the constraint literature attacks, and nothing in the underlying theory so far requires it. Against this, the proposing group continues to develop the mechanism and its phenomenology, current data do not by themselves exclude the abrupt-onset scenario, and no observation closes the window outright. What would resolve the dispute is a theoretical determination of the transition timescale, or observationally, the presence or absence of Hawking-flux signatures, in gamma rays and in CMB spectral distortions, from a transitioning population in this mass range. Because the window is the memory-burden program's flagship falsifiable prediction, its fate feeds directly into the standing of the parent mechanism, which is itself disputed.

Additional surveys of the discourse, all read as excerpts or abstracts, align with the denial side: a 2025 JCAP analysis of BBN bounds under memory burden (https://doi.org/10.1088/1475-7516/2025/11/057), a review of evaporating memory-burdened black holes identifying CMB bounds as the stronger constraint in slowly-developing scenarios (https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1475-7516/2025/11/006/pdf), a transition-sharpness analysis finding present-day fluxes require a near-instantaneous onset for a full-abundance population (arXiv:2503.21740), and an ultralight-mass bounds paper leaving only the lightest band unconstrained. On the affirmative side, the same group's follow-up (Physical Review D 110, 056029) reaffirms the window as a consequence of the mechanism, and detection-strategy papers are being written against it, so the discourse has credible voices on both sides and a one-sided verdict would manufacture resolution.

How the structure weighed. The for-side argument requires survival across cosmic time and an effectively instantaneous transition; both premises are unassessed, with seeds at 0.3 for survival and the abrupt-onset claim itself unadjudicated, and the parent mechanism stands contested at high confidence in its own right, so the for-side case cannot currently carry the claim. The against-side argument is a constraint calculation rather than a theory choice: granting a continuous transition, the established BBN and CMB bounds exclude the relevant masses from all or most of the dark matter, and the crossover corroboration subclaim seeds at 0.55. The asymmetry that decides the balance is the burden: the window needs abruptness as an additional unestablished ingredient, while the rebuttal needs only that abruptness not be assumed. That asymmetry, plus the multiplying independent negative analyses, sets credence at 0.25, close to the parent steward's seed of 0.25 reached independently; the status is contested rather than contradicted because the abrupt-onset scenario survives present data and the originating program remains active.

Limits. The full texts of the two central papers could not be retrieved this pass: stored-text fetches of the arXiv abstract and HTML pages returned access errors, and the ordinary page reader also failed on one, so the assessment rests on the abstracts and on excerpts corroborating them across independent mirrors (the search layer's five-search limit was reached). A stronger pass reading both Physical Review D papers whole, in particular how the proposal parameterizes the switch-on of suppression and how the rebuttal's exclusion threshold responds to the transition's center and duration, could sharpen the quantitative balance and is the main thing that would move this verdict; a published rebuttal re-establishing the window under a continuous transition, new flux bounds, or a rigorous derivation of the transition timescale would move it further.

The stewardship pass is complete. Summary of what was done and why:

**The claim.** "Memory burden allows primordial black holes in the 10^4 to 10^10 gram window to constitute all of the dark matter" — the flagship falsifiable prediction of the memory-burden program (Dvali and colleagues), arrived with a parent Steward's seed credence of 0.25.

**Structure.** Two named arguments, hinging on one adjudicable fact. The *for* side (abrupt-onset survival window) rests on an existing but unassessed claim that the semiclassical-to-burdened transition is practically instantaneous, plus a newly minted survival subclaim (holes of this mass range persisting across cosmic time). The *against* side (continuous-transition exclusion) rests on a newly minted conditional subclaim — BBN and recombination exclude everything below 4×10^16 grams if the transition is continuous — plus a crossover-corroboration subclaim; the same abruptness claim is attached as contradicts, so both sides of the dispute literally share the load-bearing premise. All dependencies were match-checked before minting; both new nodes were confirmed novel.

**Instances and provenance.** Three recorded: the 2024 proposal (Alexandre, Dvali, Koutsangelas, PRD 110, 036004) affirming; the 2025/2026 reanalysis (Montefalcone, Hooper, Freese, Kelso, Kühnel, Sandick, PRD 113, 023524) denying; and a 2026 smoothed-crossover BBN study as a partial denial. One response edge links the reanalysis to the proposal it rebuts. Source map written as immaterial (three sources, abstract-level reads).

**Verdict.** **Contested**, confidence 0.8, credence 0.25, marginal yield 0.35. The discourse is genuinely two-sided — the originating group maintains the window while multiple independent groups find it closed unless the transition is abrupt — but the burden of argument currently sits on the affirmative side: the window needs an abrupt, survival-capable transition that nothing yet establishes, while the rebuttal needs only that abruptness not be assumed. deltas.summary:
Memory burden, if it halts Hawking evaporation by the time a black hole has lost about half its mass, would let primordial black holes far lighter than the standard evaporation threshold survive to the present day, and the 2024 proposal by Alexandre, Dvali, and Koutsangelas (Physical Review D 110, 036004, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14069) identified the 10^4 to 10^10 gram range as a newly viable window in which such holes could constitute all of the dark matter. The claim has since become the site of a live dispute. A 2025 reanalysis by Montefalcone, Hooper, Freese, Kelso, Kühnel, and Sandick (Physical Review D 113, 023524, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.21005) recalculated the same big bang nucleosynthesis and cosmic microwave background bounds and found that the window survives only if the transition from semiclassical to burdened evaporation is practically instantaneous; under a continuous transition, [[claim:65f3b122-10de-46ec-907c-e4543c78dc83|BBN and recombination exclude everything lighter than about 4×10^16 grams from being all or most of the dark matter]], well above the proposed window. Later crossover studies reach the same qualitative conclusion with independent modeling choices, [[claim:a236aad5-5536-4caa-8957-34c62173a667|tightening the bounds and capping the window's dark matter fraction at roughly a percent in the multiplicative-crossover case]], and analyses of the transition itself find that present-day particle fluxes force the onset to be near-instantaneous for a population of this abundance.

The verdict is contested, with the burden of argument currently on the affirmative side. The window is a conditional prediction: it holds given [[claim:7ab3b712-47d8-4087-a797-6c90bc9ae58f|survival of memory-burdened holes across cosmic time]] and given [[claim:bb218573-b19d-49ae-b1e3-87fe8e234032|an effectively instantaneous handover from semiclassical to burdened evaporation]], and neither ingredient has been established; the abrupt-onset premise is the specific point the constraint literature attacks, and nothing in the underlying theory so far requires it. Against this, the proposing group continues to develop the mechanism and its phenomenology, current data do not by themselves exclude the abrupt-onset scenario, and no observation closes the window outright. What would resolve the dispute is a theoretical determination of the transition timescale, or observationally, the presence or absence of Hawking-flux signatures, in gamma rays and in CMB spectral distortions, from a transitioning population in this mass range. Because the window is the memory-burden program's flagship falsifiable prediction, its fate feeds directly into the standing of the parent mechanism, which is itself disputed.
